findings.description: At least one certificate the server sent is signed with RSA, ECDSA or EdDSA, which a cryptanalytically relevant quantum computer could forge.

references.quote: NIST will instead deprecate all quantum-vulnerable digital signature algorithms after 2030 and disallow their use under NIST standards and guidelines after 2035.

findings.remediation: Plan migration of the issuing CA hierarchy to ML-DSA (FIPS 204) or SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) certificates as client support allows.
findings.title: Certificate chain uses quantum-vulnerable signatures

findings.description: The server's handshake signature (TLS 1.3 CertificateVerify, TLS 1.2 ServerKeyExchange) used a classical scheme, so its authentication relies on a quantum-vulnerable key.

references.quote: NIST will instead deprecate all quantum-vulnerable digital signature algorithms after 2030 and disallow their use under NIST standards and guidelines after 2035.

findings.remediation: Deploy an ML-DSA certificate and key for clients that support it.
findings.title: Server authenticates with a quantum-vulnerable signature

findings.description: The negotiated key exchange is not based on ML-KEM-1024 (security category 5). NIST recommends ML-KEM-768 by default; some policies (for example CNSA 2.0) require ML-KEM-1024.

references.quote: NIST recommends using ML-KEM-768 as the default parameter set, as it provides a large security margin at a reasonable performance cost. In cases where this is impractical or when higher security is required, other parameter sets may be used.

findings.remediation: Where the applicable policy requires ML-KEM-1024, enable SecP384r1MLKEM1024 or MLKEM1024 and prefer it.
findings.title: Key exchange does not use ML-KEM-1024

score.method: 100 minus 0 per info, 2 per low, 10 per medium, 25 per high and 50 per critical finding, floored at 0; capped at 40 if any finding is critical. Rules listed in not_evaluated do not affect the score.

certificate_chain.basis: 0 of 1 certificate signature algorithms are ML-DSA, SLH-DSA or composite ML-DSA OIDs

handshake_signature.basis: server signature scheme ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256 is classical

key_exchange.basis: negotiated group X25519MLKEM768 (0x11ec) is hybrid in the IANA TLS Supported Groups registry
